notes: 1. Admin master OTP = 258369; UAT admin mobile = 8888888888. The master OTP works for any registered admin mobile on UAT and bypasses real SMS delivery.
2. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] = a disposable UAT account/state (e.g. an isActive=false admin user, or a valid API bearer token) must be supplied before executing this test.
3. [VERIFY WITH DEV] = behaviour not confirmed in BRD/FRD/FS; confirm before treating Pass/Fail as authoritative.
4. Auth is Mobile-OTP only (no password). Step 1 = mobile entry, Step 2 = 6-box OTP entry. Successful login redirects to /admin/customers. JWT session lasts ~1 day (1d expiry).

5. SECURITY GAPS (documented, not yet fixed): Logout is a server-side no-op — the JWT stays valid until natural 1-day expiry (do NOT test post-logout 401 as a pass). No backend OTP cooldown and no wrong-OTP lockout — the 60s re-send gate is UI-only. OTP is generated with Math.random() and stored plaintext. Master OTP has no production gate.

6. API request field is `phone` (not `mobile`) and the JWT is returned wrapped as response.data.token — this matches the live implementation in visual-memory; the FRD/FS examples still say `mobile`/flat token and are stale (see DOC_DRIFT-001 / DOC_DRIFT-002).

tcs.scenario: To verify OTP is generated with insecure Math.random()

2. Analyse the distribution / predictability.
tcs.expected: OTP is generated via Math.floor(100000 + Math.random() * 900000) — NOT crypto.randomInt or an equivalent CSPRNG (auth.controller.js:52-54). Document as a known security gap; recommend migrating to crypto.randomInt.

tcs.scenario: To verify the session persists across a page refresh
tcs.description: Verify that refreshing the page keeps the admin logged in.
tcs.precond: The admin is logged in.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in successfully.
2. Press F5 to refresh.
tcs.expected: The admin stays logged in; the page reloads without redirecting to login.

tcs.scenario: To verify the session persists in a new tab
tcs.description: Verify that opening a protected URL in a new tab of the same browser does not prompt for login.
tcs.precond: The admin is logged in.
tcs.steps:
1. Open a new tab in the same browser.
2. Go to /admin/customers.
tcs.expected: The new tab loads the page directly without a login prompt.

tcs.scenario: To verify the session survives browser restart within the JWT window
tcs.description: Verify that closing and reopening the browser within the 1-day window keeps the session.
tcs.precond: The admin is logged in and the JWT is stored in localStorage.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in successfully.
2. Close the browser completely.
3. Reopen the browser.
4. Go to /admin/customers.
tcs.expected: The session is restored from localStorage and the Customers page loads without redirecting to login.

tcs.scenario: To verify the session lasts up to 1 day
tcs.description: Verify that the session remains valid within the 1-day JWT window.
tcs.precond: The admin is logged in and a JWT has been issued.
tcs.steps:
1. Note the login time.
2. Wait 23 hours.
3. Access a protected route.
tcs.expected: The session is still valid within the 24-hour window.

tcs.scenario: To verify behaviour at the exact JWT expiry boundary
tcs.description: Verify that the session is rejected at/after the JWT's 1-day exp claim and the user is sent to login.
tcs.precond: The admin has a JWT close to its 1-day expiry. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] an aged/short-expiry token.
tcs.steps:
1. Use a JWT at/just past its exp.
2. Access a protected route.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] BRD states the session lasts 1 day; the exact at-expiry behaviour and clock-skew tolerance are not documented. [To verify] confirm the request is rejected (401) and the user is redirected to /admin at/after exp.

tcs.scenario: To verify a second-device login does not invalidate the first
tcs.description: Verify that logging in on a second device leaves the first device's session intact (stateless JWT).
tcs.precond: The admin is logged in on Device A.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in as the same admin on Device B.
2. Return to Device A.
3. Access /admin/customers.
tcs.expected: Both devices stay authenticated — the JWT is stateless and not bound to one device, and no session blacklist exists (per FS Feature 3 §6).

tcs.scenario: To verify direct URL is the only route to login
tcs.description: Verify that hitting the login URL or a protected route without a session both resolve to the login page.
tcs.precond: No active session.
tcs.steps:
1. Access /admin without a session.
2. Try /admin/customers directly.
tcs.expected: Both routes resolve to the login page.

tcs.scenario: To verify an expired session redirects to login
tcs.description: Verify that an expired/cleared session forces a redirect to the login page.
tcs.precond: The session token is expired or cleared.
tcs.steps:
1. Clear the stored admin session.
2. Try to access /admin/customers.
tcs.expected: The user is redirected to the /admin login page.

tcs.scenario: To verify a protected route without login redirects
tcs.description: Verify that accessing a protected route with no session redirects to login.
tcs.precond: No active session.
tcs.steps:
1. Open an incognito window.
2. Go to /admin/towers.
tcs.expected: The user is redirected to the /admin login page.

tcs.scenario: To verify a tampered JWT forces a redirect to login
tcs.description: Verify that editing the stored JWT causes the protected API call to fail and the user to be sent to login.
tcs.precond: The admin is logged in.
tcs.steps:
1. Open DevTools, Application, localStorage.
2. Change a character in the JWT payload.
3. Reload /admin/customers.
tcs.expected: The API call fails with 401 and the user is redirected to the /admin login page.

tcs.scenario: To verify Logout redirects to the login page
tcs.description: Verify that clicking Logout clears the client session and returns the user to the login page.
tcs.precond: The admin is logged in.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the user/profile menu in the top-right.
2. Click Logout.
3. Observe the resulting screen.
tcs.expected: The browser redirects to /admin (login page) and the local session is cleared. (Note: this is a client-side redirect — the JWT itself is NOT invalidated server-side; see ADM_LGN_FSD_045.)

tcs.scenario: To verify Logout does not invalidate the JWT server-side
tcs.description: Verify the documented critical security gap that the JWT remains usable after Logout until natural expiry.
tcs.precond: The admin is logged in with an active JWT. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Capture the JWT bearer token.
2. POST /api/v1/auth/logout with the bearer token (expect 200).
3. Immediately call a protected endpoint (e.g. GET /api/v1/admin/dashboard/all-buyers) with the same JWT.
tcs.expected: Step 2 returns 200 'Logged out successfully'. Step 3 STILL returns 200 — the JWT is stateless with no server-side blacklist, so the token stays valid until its exp claim (default 1d). (auth.controller.js:36-46.) QA must NOT write a post-logout 401 pass case.

tcs.scenario: To verify a revoked (inactive) user is blocked
tcs.description: Verify that a user whose access has been revoked (isActive=false) is rejected at verify with the exact message.
tcs.precond: A disposable UAT admin user exists with isActive=false. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] revoked user.
tcs.steps:
1. Send OTP for the revoked admin mobile.
2. Enter the master OTP and Submit.
3. Read the error.
tcs.expected: Verify-OTP returns HTTP 400 with the exact text 'Your access to the portal has been revoked' (FS §11.4); the user is not logged in. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the UI surfaces this exact string inline.

tcs.scenario: To verify OTP is delivered via Epinet SMS (not Kaleyra)
tcs.description: Verify that the OTP SMS is dispatched through Epinet and NOT Kaleyra. [BUG-REF: BUG-AUTH-002]
tcs.precond: Backend outbound network-log capture is available; a valid admin mobile. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] backend log access.
tcs.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/auth/admin/send-otp with phone 8888888888.
2. Inspect the backend's outbound HTTP traffic.
tcs.expected: Outbound SMS hits https://epinetinfo.in/api/pushsms with user 'HOABLDIGITAL', DLT template id 1007393289666667759, recipient 918888888888. There is NO call to Kaleyra. (services/api/whatsapp.service.js:92-122.)

tcs.scenario: To verify send is fire-and-forget (success even on dispatch failure)
tcs.description: Verify the documented gap that send-otp returns success even when the outbound SMS dispatch fails.
tcs.precond: Backend with a simulated outbound failure to epinet/botspice. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] network-fault injection.
tcs.steps:
1. Block outbound DNS to epinetinfo.in and the botspice endpoints.
2. POST send-otp for the admin.
tcs.expected: The backend returns 200 'OTP sent successfully' even though no message actually left the system; the user row still has otp and otpExpires set. (Send calls are NOT awaited — auth.controller.js:590-600.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the lastLogin assignment is silently dropped
tcs.description: Verify the documented inconsistency that user.lastLogin assignment is a no-op when the column is absent.
tcs.precond: An admin successfully logs in. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] DB schema access.
tcs.steps:
1. Complete a successful login.
2. Check whether a last_login column exists on users.
tcs.expected: The column may or may not exist depending on migrations. The user.lastLogin = new Date() assignment (auth.controller.js:859-861) is a silent no-op when the column is absent — Sequelize drops unknown attributes. Document the inconsistency.

tcs.scenario: To verify there is no backend OTP cooldown
tcs.description: Verify the documented gap that send-otp has no server-side rate limit (the 60s gate is UI-only).
tcs.precond: An API client is available. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Call send-otp for the admin mobile.
2. Immediately call send-otp again, back-to-back, several times.
tcs.expected: Every back-to-back send-otp call succeeds — there is NO server-side cooldown (the throttle block at auth.controller.js:558-568 is commented out). The 60s re-send gate exists only on the UI (BRD §6 Rule 4 / FS Feature 1 §6). Document the gap; do not test backend cooldown as a passing case.
